title: Seat a cocked tri-clamp square on both ferrules before drawing it up with its wing nut
instruction: Tighten the clamp on the pipe joint.
context: Process technicians and food, beverage and pharmaceutical machine operators (O*NET 51-9012.00, 51-3092.00) make up sanitary (tri-clamp) joints many times a shift: two ferrules meet face to face on a gasket, a hinged clamp ring with a tapered channel goes round both flanges, and a wing nut on its swing bolt is turned hand tight, so the taper draws the ferrules onto the gasket. The clamp must sit square with both flanges inside its channel all round before the nut is drawn up. A clamp tightened while cocked, its lip riding on a flange rim, bites the rim on one side and leaves the joint open on the other: it leaks and can blow off under line pressure, and the gasket must be replaced. A nut left at contact seeps, and one cranked far past hand tight squeezes the gasket into the bore, where product lodges. Here the clamp went on cocked, its hinge side up on the rims, with the nut 1.5 turns loose.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. A painted steel pipe stand is fixed to the table: a base plate 17 x 10 x 1.2 cm centered at x 29.5, y 4.5, and a 2.5 cm square post at x 36.5, y 4.5 11.1 cm tall with a 9 x 2 x 1 cm arm at z 11.8 that straps round the upper spool. The process line is 1.5-inch sanitary stainless tube (38.1 mm OD, 1.65 mm wall), vertical on the axis x 26, y 4.5. The lower ferrule (50.5 mm flange, 2.85 mm thick at the rim, 20-degree tapered back) is welded to a tube stub standing on the plate, its face at z 8.95; the upper ferrule ends a short spool held by the bracket, its face at z 9.05 and its cut end open at z 13.0. A white PTFE tri-clamp gasket (50.5 mm OD, 35 mm bore) lies centered between the two faces. The clamp is a single-hinge 1.5-inch tri-clamp in cast stainless: a ring 62 mm across and 14 mm tall with a channel 53 mm across and 9 mm tall inside and lips with a 44 mm bore, its two halves hinged on the robot's side (knuckle at x 22.55) and closed at two ears on the far side, 6 mm thick and 3 mm apart at contact. An M8 x 1.25 swing bolt pinned in the ear on the robot's right (-y) runs along y through the slotted ear on its left at x 31.0, z 9.0, and carries a brass wing nut (36 mm across the wings, wings 10 mm thick, lying flat) on its +y end, 1.5 turns short of touching the ear (its hub's center at y 5.94; at contact y 5.75). The clamp starts cocked: its far side is in place over both flanges, but it is tilted 6 degrees about the swing bolt's axis, so its hinge side is 8.7 mm high with its lower lip resting on top of the upper ferrule's rim instead of under the lower one. Both arms start at home.
scoring: Scored at the end of the run, with a history kept over the whole run. Square means the clamp's tilt is under 0.8 degrees: its hinge side within 1.05 mm of square, inside the channel's 1.15 mm of axial play over the flange pair, so both flanges and the gasket are in the channel all round. Past contact means the wing nut is more than 10 degrees (0.035 mm of bolt travel) past touching the ear. Drawn up cocked: if the nut is ever past contact while the clamp is not square (at that control step or the one before), the score is 0 and stays 0 (the lip has bitten the rim and the gasket must be replaced), even if the nut is backed off and the clamp reseated. Also 0: the clamp not square at the end; a gripper still holding the nut, or any gripper's tool point within 6 cm of the joint's center or 4 cm of the nut; the nut not past contact; or more than 90 degrees of its tightening done without a gripper holding it and turning with it (a knock or swipe). Otherwise: 0.25 if the nut was ever more than 1.5 turns past contact (past firm hand tight, the gasket is squeezed into the bore; backing off does not undo it); 0.5 if it is past contact but under half a turn (0.6 mm of bolt travel: the ferrules are not yet drawn onto the gasket and it seeps under pressure); 1.0 from half a turn to 1.5 turns with both arms home and still (tool points within 3 cm of their start), else 0.9. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.9, 1.0. A real trial is checked with a feeler gauge between the clamp's lips and the flange back faces at the hinge and at the ears (equal within 1 mm), a paint mark on the wing nut against one on the bolt counted from the contact mark, and the top video for the order of pressing and tightening.
reset_notes: Back the wing nut off to 1.5 turns short of the ear (a paint mark on the nut and bolt), lift the clamp's hinge side so its lower lip rests on top of the upper ferrule's rim, and check the gasket for a crushed bead or a bulge into the bore (replace it if either).
fidelity: The stand, ferrules and gasket are fixed. The clamp is one rigid ring on a hinge about its swing bolt's axis, with a model law: it rests cocked on the rim until its high side is pressed down 1.5 degrees, then drops square, and it is held where it is once the nut is past contact; the halves' closing (under 1 mm) is not drawn. The wing nut is a thread model (twistkit); its wings are drawn 10 mm thick so the fingers close on them.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps; both hands hover near home, never reach the joint); demo: 1.0 (1,258 steps)
